openings.claim: Unreliable reservation identities and storage addresses may explain delays. Retain surname shelving, dividers and cart; update the behind-desk locator when books move, distinguishing household surnames from reservation identity.
openings.discriminator: Matched accurate addresses should reduce second searches and retrieval time. If searching shortens but peak waiting dominates, the arrival burst is the stronger explanation; match cart volume and book size.
openings.probe: Clerk compares locator updates with usual practice, recording arrival, service start, retrieval, completion, address accuracy and second searches on existing paper.
openings.uncertainty: Synthetic stipulations establish no effect. Existing identity-check capability, household-mismatch causality, sustained update feasibility and target attainment are unconfirmed.

openings.claim: Shelving may create a feedback loop: relocation stales the exception slip, prompting second searches and further corrections. Keep a bounded already-fitting cart batch stationary through evening, deferring shelving until afterward.
openings.discriminator: Against usual movement, matched stationary batches should reduce stale entries, second searches and slow pickups. Equal failures or erased cart advantage favor independent recording errors, household mismatches or sample selection.
openings.probe: Clerk compares stationary and usual-movement evenings, recording movements, second searches, pickup times, handoff errors, arrival mix and congestion.
openings.uncertainty: Relocation causality, comparable samples within the preparation budget, broader cart capacity and deployment benefit remain unproven.

lineage.reason: Preserves locator repair and the competing burst explanation.
Preserves the distinct relocation feedback test.

decision: Run bounded comparisons using only the existing evening clerk, two shelves, one cart, paper and timing sheet. Keep names/contact details behind the desk and verify recipients. Daily preparation, setup and preparation corrections must total at most ten clerk-minutes; record update work and stop if the cap fails. Assess at least 95% within two minutes and zero wrong-reader handoffs separately; any wrong handoff defeats fit. Reader-interview representativeness remains unknown.
